sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises steadily as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk rises with it, with the largest rise between none and one or more.
The effect of utilization grows with the number of past delinquencies: a high utilization adds far more risk for applicants who have delinquencies than for those who have none.
Income is among the third or fourth most important drivers, and higher income generally lowers the risk of default.
Length of credit history is also among the third or fourth most important drivers, and longer histories generally lower the risk.
Debt-to-income ratio has at most a weak effect, with higher ratios raising the risk somewhat.
The number of recent credit inquiries and the number of dependents have at most a weak effect, and the data do not settle whether the number of dependents matters at all.
The applicant's age hardly matters for the model's predictions.
